subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Transistor: The Tiny Switch That Built the Future
description: A fast breakdown of The Transistor: The Tiny Switch That Built the Future for builders.

hook.text: The first computer filled a room and used 18,000 vacuum tubes. Each tube burned out every few hours.

buildup.text: In 1947, Bell Labs invented the transistor — a tiny switch made of semiconductor material.

discovery.text: Transistors don't burn out, use almost no power, and can be shrunk to nanometer scale.

twist.text: Bell Labs gave the technology away through licensing. They thought it was only good for hearing aids.

climax.text: Today, a single chip holds 50 billion transistors. Every phone, car, and appliance depends on them.

punchline.text: The most important invention was too small to see.

quiz.question: What did Bell Labs initially think the transistor was best suited for?
options: Military radar systems for the Cold War
Hearing aids and small amplifier devices
